'''Juan C. Meza''' is an American mathematician, electrical engineer, and university professor.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Juan Meza Named One of Hispanic Business Magazine's "100 Influentials" |url=https://cs.lbl.gov/news-media/news/news-archive/2009/juan-meza-named-one-of-hispanic-business-magazine-s-100-influentials/ |access-date=2023-04-29 |website=Berkeley Lab Computing Sciences |language=en
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210328152016/https://cs.lbl.gov/news-media/news/news-archive/2009/juan-meza-named-one-of-hispanic-business-magazine-s-100-influentials/|archivedate=March 28, 2021}}</ref><ref name=UCMerced-NatSci-Meza>{{cite web
|accessdate=March 12, 2025|url=https://naturalsciences.ucmerced.edu/people/juan-c-meza-0
|title=Juan C. Meza, Professor, Applied Math|publisher=Department of Natural Sciences, UC Merced}}</ref> He is recognized for his contributions to [[computational mathematics]], [[high-performance computing]], and his advocacy for equity and representation in [[Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics|STEM]] fields.<ref name=":0" />

Meza is currently a Professor of Applied Mathematics at [[University of California, Merced]] (UC Merced)<ref name=UCMerced-AMSfellow2020>{{cite web|accessdate=March 8, 2025|url=https://news.ucmerced.edu/news/2020/meza-named-first-ams-fellow-uc-merced|title=Meza Named First AMS Fellow from UC Merced|date=November 6, 2020|work=Newsroom|publisher=UC Merced}}</ref> and the Associate Director for the [[Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute]].<ref name=SLMath-Meza>{{cite web|accessdate=March 12, 2025
|url=https://www.slmath.org/people/48557|title=Juan C. Meza|publisher=Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute (SLMath)}}</ref> He had previously served as the Dean of the School of Natural Sciences at the UC Merced (2011-2017).<ref name=UCMerced-AMSfellow2020/><ref name=SLMath-Meza/>

He is received numerous awards and has served on several prestigious scientific and computational mathematics boards and commissions.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Diaz-Lopez |first1=Alexander |last2=Harris |first2=Pamela E. |last3=Prieto Langarica |first3=Alicia |last4=Sosa |first4=Gabriel |title=Lathisms:Latin@s and Hispanics in Mathematical Sciences |url=https://www.ams.org/publications/journals/notices/201609/rnoti-p1019.pdf |journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society |date=2016 |volume=63 |issue=9 |pages=1024 |doi=10.1090/noti1425 |doi-access=free}}</ref> At the federal level, he served on advisory committees for the [[National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine|National Research Council]], the [[Department of Energy]] (DOE), and the [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF).<ref name=MezaProfile>{{cite web|accessdate=March 12, 2025|url=https://www.juancmeza.com/about|title=Juan Meza}}</ref>
== Education ==
Meza attained all his degrees exclusively from [[Rice University]]. He earned his B.S. in electrical engineering in 1978 and, in 1979, a M.S. in the same field. He was conferred a PhD, M.A. in 1986 in Computational and Applied Mathematics from the same university.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Juan C Meza {{!}} University of California, Merced - Academia.edu |url=https://ucmerced.academia.edu/JuanMeza/CurriculumVitae |access-date=2023-05-22 |website=ucmerced.academia.edu}}</ref> His doctoral advisor was William Woodbury Symes.

== Career ==
In his career, Meza made an impression in the world of math, technology, and science. Earlier in his life, Meza worked in the [[Sandia National Laboratories]], where he served as a Distinguished Member of the Technical Staff, a recognition only a few had received before him. Later as the chief scientist at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], he also became the head of computational research in the field of mathematics.<ref name=":0" /> Meza later joined the [[University of California, Merced]] as a professor in applied mathematics and became a dean of the School of Natural Sciences.<ref name=":1" /> In this role, Meza focused on improving the School of Natural Science's accessibility to marginalized people of color, promoting equity and inclusion in the fields of computational science and hiring diverse faculty to honor representation.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=School of Natural Sciences Dean Set to Begin New Leadership Position {{!}} Panorama |url=http://panorama.ucmerced.edu/news/school-natural-sciences-dean-set-begin-new-leadership-position |access-date=2023-05-23 |website=panorama.ucmerced.edu}}</ref> 

== Awards and recognition ==
Meza won the [[Blackwell–Tapia prize|Blackwell Tapia Award]] for his exceptional services in computational and applied mathematics in 2008 for earnestly promoting participation and contribution from scientists and mathematicians from marginalized communities of color.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Buckmire |first=Ron |date=February 2019 |title=Recognizing Black and Latinx Mathematical Excellence: The Blackwell-Tapia Prize |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201902/rnoti-p218.pdf |journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society |volume=66 |issue=2 |pages=218–220 |doi=10.1090/noti1798 |doi-access=free}}</ref> He also received recognition as the Top 100 Influential in the ''Hispanic Business'' magazine. To honor Meza's contribution towards the success of underrepresented and marginalized students, he was conferred the [[Society for the Advancement of Chicanos/Hispanics and Native Americans in Science|Society for Advancement of Chicanos and Native Americans in Science]] (SACNAS) Distinguished Scientist Award.<ref name=":0" /> He also received the Gordon Bell Prize in 2008 and in 2022, Meza was awarded the [[Richard Tapia Celebration of Diversity in Computing|Richard Tapia Achievement Award for Scientific Scholarship, Civic Science, and Diversifying Computing]] for his advocacy for equity and diversity in computational mathematics and science. The conference theme was " A Time to Celebrate Resilience, Adaptability, and Innovation in Computing."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Small |first=Ashley |date=2022-05-12 |title=UC Merced Applied Mathematics Professor Dr. Juan C. Meza Receives The Richard Tapia Achievement Award |url=https://cmd-it.org/news-recent/uc-merced-applied-mathematics-professor-dr-juan-c-meza-receives-the-richard-tapia-achievement-award/ |access-date=2023-05-22 |website=CMD-IT |language=en-US}}</ref> His other awards include the Rice University Outstanding Engineering Alumni Award.<ref name=":2" />

== Committees ==
In his career, Meza has served on several boards and commissions. Some include the National Research Council Board on Mathematical Sciences and Their Applications, National Partnership for Advanced Computational Infrastructure, and the Human Resources Advisory Committee for the Mathematical Sciences Research Institute. He has also sat on a board of governors for the [[Institute for Mathematics and its Applications]].<ref name=":1" />
